# 7-Day Sleep and Energy Self-Care Plan

A simple, non-emergency routine can help with both sleep quality and daytime energy while keeping allergies and heartburn in mind. This plan stays under **$40** by focusing on a few low-cost OTC options plus habit changes.

## Best Low-Complexity Options for Your Situation

| Option | What it helps | Typical use | Cost fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Saline nasal spray or rinse** | Seasonal allergy congestion that disrupts sleep | Evening and as needed | Low |
| **Non-sedating antihistamine** such as loratadine or fexofenadine | Allergy symptoms without drowsiness | Once daily during allergy days | Low to moderate |
| **Alginate or antacid** for heartburn | Nighttime reflux that can wake you up | After trigger meals or before bed if needed | Low |
| **Low-dose melatonin** | Sleep timing, not a sedative | 30–60 minutes before bed for a short trial | Low |
| **Magnesium glycinate** if tolerated | Relaxation and sleep support | Evening, with food | Moderate |

## 7-Day Basic Schedule

| Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening / Bedtime |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | Wake at the same time; get 10–15 min of outdoor light | Keep caffeine only before noon | No food 2–3 hours before bed; saline spray if congested |
| **2** | Hydrate; light breakfast with protein | Short walk after lunch | Use non-sedating antihistamine if allergy symptoms are active |
| **3** | Same wake time; avoid snoozing | Limit late sugar and heavy meals | Try a heartburn-friendly dinner; elevate head slightly if needed |
| **4** | 5–10 min movement soon after waking | Take a brief break from screens every 60–90 min | Consider melatonin for 2–3 nights if falling asleep is the main issue |
| **5** | Repeat light exposure and hydration | Keep lunch moderate, not greasy | Use saline rinse/spray before bed if nasal symptoms are present |
| **6** | Same wake time; no long naps | Walk or stretch after work | If heartburn happens, use antacid or alginate per label directions |
| **7** | Review which habits helped most | Keep caffeine cutoff and lunch walk | Repeat the simplest winning bedtime routine |

## Practical Precautions

- **Avoid sedating antihistamines** like diphenhydramine or doxylamine if you want better daytime energy.
- **Do not combine multiple sleep aids** on the same night unless a pharmacist or clinician has told you it is okay.
- **Use melatonin briefly and lightly**; more is not necessarily better.
- **Watch heartburn triggers**: late meals, alcohol, spicy foods, fatty foods, and lying down soon after eating.
- **Stop and get medical advice** if you have chest pain, trouble breathing, black stools, vomiting blood, severe reflux, loud snoring with choking, or sleep problems that persist despite routine changes.

## Simple $40 OTC Starter Pack

- **Saline nasal spray/rinse**: about $5–$10
- **Non-sedating antihistamine**: about $10–$20
- **Antacid or alginate**: about $5–$10
- **Low-dose melatonin**: about $5–$10

A basic combo usually fits your budget if you choose only what matches your symptoms.

- Sleep hygiene guidance: https://www.sleepfoundation.org/sleep-hygiene

- GERD and heartburn basics: https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/acid-reflux-ger-gerd-adults
- Medication pricing reference: https://www.goodrx.com/
